newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Golden boy of right eager for Slovenia power.
newsitem.headline: Golden boy of right eager for Slovenia power.

text.p: Marjan Podobnik, Slovenia's youngest party leader at 36, heads an alliance of rightwing parties aiming to thwart any chance of centre-left Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek returning to power.

Slovenian President Milan Kucan on Monday nominated Drnovsek to form the next government after inconclusive general elections on November 10 but warned that the positions of the political parties were becoming entrenched with neither side willing to support the other.

Podobnik, who entered politics nine years ago as co-founder of the first non-communist party to be registered in former Yugoslavia, vowed after the November election that he would become prime minister.

Now leader of the conservative, pro-farmers' People's Party, Podobnik pushed to set up an alliance of right-wing parties to create what he called a viable alternative to Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats.
The alliance, which includes the centre-right Social Democrats and Christian Democrats, almost clinched victory, just missing an absolute parliamentary majority by one seat.
The People's Party is the biggest among the alliance, winning 19 seats in the 90-member parliament. The alliance together won 45 seats.
A father of three children, Podobnik is a strong believer in the Roman Catholic church and family values.

Trained as an agricultural engineer, he co-founded the Slovenian Farmer's Union in 1988, the first party to be allowed to stand against Yugoslavia's ruling communists and won a seat in parliament in 1990.
The Union changed its name to the People's Party in 1992, and Podobnik became its leader. His brother, Janez, 37, is deputy leader and current speaker of parliament.

While supporting entry into the European Union, Podobnik has called for a cautious approach to full membership, arguing that Slovenia had to have guarantees that its national interests, and farmers in particular, would be protected.
The People's Party unconditionally backs NATO membership, as do the other parties in the rightist alliance.

Podobnik has called for a quicker approach to privatisation but the process may become bogged down if the right-wing parties carry out their proposal to review past privatisations to check for irregularities.
Podobnik, dubbed the karaoke kid in the Slovenian press, showed a lighter side to his character before the general election by cutting a CD of him singing popular songs.
